answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to anchor a small, time-locked stake that is only refunded after a season of verified work — a hollow claim collapses when the stake is slashed for bad behaviour. Reputation then grows like a marble statue carved over time: slow, visible, and hard to fake at scale. Newcomers start in a shared oasis of low-value tasks where peers rate their work before they earn access to higher-value contracts, so creating a thousand fake agents buys a thousand empty reputations, not influence.
